title: bvy25 with the type's level compensation OFF (bv_comp 0): the type is a plain value sort
question: Is bvy25's gap carried by the type being hidden in value at y = 0? With no compensation, higher-exposure types are worth less and size reveals the type monotonically.
notes: VISIBILITY LADDER (2026-10-10), point 1 of 2. bvy25 (bv_comp 1.2) has a fair gap of +0.0148 with the KP14 signature: a linear fit on the ranks explains 44-59% of the true premium, type dummies 94%, and room_s is 96% of room. The reduced-form screen's one working lever is curvature of the premium in the ranks, and KP14's measured footprint says its gap is a static rank-nonlinearity of the growth-option share WITHIN a type. This ladder asks what the compensation does: at bv_comp 0 the type is a monotone level sort of value (the GS21 situation), at 1.0 it is exactly invisible at y = 0, at 1.2 (bvy25) slightly over-compensated.\n\nPREDICTION (2026-10-10, before the run): the type becomes linearly visible in size, the linear benchmark takes more of the premium, room falls below bvy25's +0.062 and the fair gap falls below +0.008. FALSIFIED if the fair gap stays at or above bvy25's +0.0148 (then visibility is not the mechanism). Same seeds, same solve machinery as bvy25; the J* table is rebuilt because type_theta enters it.
